The number of lone pairs on bromine in \(\ce{BrF3}\) is:

text_solutions: In \(\ce{BrF3}\), bromine has 7 valence electrons and forms 3 single bonds (6 electrons used), leaving 4 electrons as 2 lone pairs. With \(sp^3d\) hybridization, the 5 electron pairs (3 bonding, 2 lone) result in a T-shaped molecular geometry.

qns_content.text: The bond angle in \( \ce{H2S} \) is approximately:

text_solutions: In \( \ce{H2S} \), sulfur is \( sp^3 \) hybridized with two lone pairs, reducing the bond angle to about 92° due to lone pair repulsion.

qns_content.text: The bond in \( \ce{HCl} \) is an example of:

text_solutions: In \( \ce{HCl} \), hydrogen and chlorine share one electron pair, forming a single covalent bond.

qns_content.text: Which molecule has an equatorial bond angle of approximately 101° due to a lone pair?

text_solutions: In \(\ce{SF4}\), sulfur is \(sp^3d\) hybridized with 5 electron pairs (4 bonding, 1 lone), forming a see-saw shape. The equatorial F-S-F bond angle is ~101° due to lone pair repulsion compressing the equatorial bonds.

qns_content.text: The number of sigma bonds in \( \ce{C3H6} \) (cyclopropane) is:

text_solutions: In \( \ce{C3H6} \) (cyclopropane), there are 3 \( \ce{C-C} \) sigma bonds in the ring and 6 \( \ce{C-H} \) sigma bonds, totaling 9 sigma bonds.

qns_content.text: Which molecule has a linear geometry due to \( sp \) hybridization?

text_solutions: In \( \ce{C2H2} \), each carbon is \( sp \) hybridized, forming a triple bond and a linear structure with a 180° bond angle.

qns_content.text: Which molecule has a trigonal planar electron pair geometry and a trigonal planar molecular shape?

text_solutions: In \( \ce{BCl3} \), boron has 3 bonding pairs and no lone pairs with \( sp^2 \) hybridization, giving a trigonal planar electron and molecular geometry.

qns_content.text: Which molecule has an incomplete octet with only 6 electrons around the central atom?

text_solutions: In \( \ce{AlCl3} \), aluminum forms three bonds, using 6 electrons, resulting in an incomplete octet.

qns_content.text: The total number of sigma bonds in \( \ce{C6H6} \) (benzene) is:

text_solutions: In \( \ce{C6H6} \) (benzene), there are 6 \( \ce{C-C} \) sigma bonds in the ring, 6 \( \ce{C-H} \) sigma bonds, totaling 12 sigma bonds (plus 3 pi bonds).

qns_content.text: The strongest type of bond in terms of bond dissociation energy is:

text_solutions: A triple bond, as in \( \ce{N2} \) (bond enthalpy ~946 kJ/mol), is the strongest due to three shared electron pairs.

qns_content.text: Which of the following has a triple bond?

text_solutions: In \( \ce{C2H2} \) (ethyne), the carbon atoms share three electron pairs, forming a triple bond (1 sigma + 2 pi).

qns_content.text: Which molecule violates the octet rule by having more than 8 electrons around the central atom and involves d-orbital hybridization?

text_solutions: In \( \ce{SF6} \), sulfur has 6 bonds (12 electrons) with \( sp^3d^2 \) hybridization, exceeding the octet using d-orbitals.

qns_content.text: The bond order of \( \ce{H2} \) molecule according to molecular orbital theory is:

text_solutions: For \( \ce{H2} \), electronic configuration is \( (\sigma 1s)^2 \). Bond order = \( \frac{2 - 0}{2} = 1 \).

qns_content.text: Which molecule has the shortest bond length among those with a double bond?

text_solutions: Among molecules with a double bond, \(\ce{O2}\) has a bond length of ~121 pm, shorter than \(\ce{C2H4}\) (~134 pm), \(\ce{SO2}\) (~143 pm), or \(\ce{NO2}\) (~124 pm), due to higher bond strength and smaller atomic radii.

qns_content.text: Which molecule contains a single bond with a bond length of approximately 154 pm?

text_solutions: In \( \ce{C2H6} \) (ethane), the \( \ce{C-C} \) single bond has a bond length of ~154 pm, typical for carbon-carbon single bonds.

qns_content.text: The number of sigma bonds in \( \ce{C4H10} \) (butane) is:

qns_content.text: Which species is diamagnetic and has a bond order of 3?

text_solutions: For \( \ce{N2} \): \( (\sigma 1s)^2 (\sigma^* 1s)^2 (\sigma 2s)^2 (\sigma^* 2s)^2 (\pi 2p_x)^2 (\pi 2p_y)^2 (\sigma 2p_z)^2 \). Bonding = 10, antibonding = 4. Bond order = \( \frac{10 - 4}{2} = 3 \), with all electrons paired (diamagnetic).
